prompt:
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Investigate ledger-sync on 2026-05-07, reference 10:00–11:00 versus incident 11:00–12:00. For every period and serving physical pool report operations, terminal failures and percentage, attempts, failed attempts and percentage, retried operations, minimum/maximum applied deadline_ms, and mean queue_ms and execution_ms of the terminal attempt among terminally failed operations. Report means of every recorded telemetry signal for those pools and applied changes during 10:00–12:00 (kind, pool, effective time, before/after JSON strings). In assessment identify the strongest supported proximal explanation, the affected pool and failure increase in pp. Explicitly evaluate both a deadline-policy change and worker/queue pressure against the current evidence. Explain the remaining causal limitation.

arguments.command:
cd /data; cat > /work/ls.sql <<'EOF'
with ops as (select o.operation_id, o.route_id, o.opened_at_ms, case when o.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 and o.opened_at_ms<1778151600000 then 'reference_10_11' when o.opened_at_ms>=1778151600000 and o.opened_at_ms<1778155200000 then 'incident_11_12' end period
 from logical_operations o join service_routes r using(route_id) join services s on s.service_id=r.service_id where s.service_code='ledger-sync' and o.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 and o.opened_at_ms<1778155200000),
asg as (select ops.*, ra.pool_id, ra.profile_id from ops join route_assignments ra on ra.route_id=ops.route_id and ops.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms and ops.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms),
att as (select a.operation_id, count(*) n, sum(f.is_success=0) failed from attempt_events a join failure_codes f using(code_id) group by a.operation_id),
lst as (select a.operation_id, f.is_success last_ok, a.queue_ms, a.execution_ms from attempt_events a join failure_codes f using(code_id) where a.attempt_no=(select max(b.attempt_no) from attempt_events b where b.operation_id=a.operation_id))
select asg.period, p.pool_code, count(*) operations, sum(lst.last_ok=0) terminal_failures, round(100.0*sum(lst.last_ok=0)/count(*),4) terminal_failure_pct,
 sum(att.n) attempts, sum(att.failed) failed_attempts, round(100.0*sum(att.failed)/sum(att.n),4) attempt_failure_pct, sum(att.n>1) retried_operations,
 min(d.deadline_ms) min_deadline_ms, max(d.deadline_ms) max_deadline_ms,
 round(avg(case when lst.last_ok=0 then lst.queue_ms end),4) failed_terminal_queue_mean_ms, round(avg(case when lst.last_ok=0 then lst.execution_ms end),4) failed_terminal_execution_mean_ms
from asg join worker_pools p using(pool_id) join policy_profiles d on d.profile_id=asg.profile_id join att using(operation_id) join lst using(operation_id) where asg.period is not null group by asg.period, p.pool_code order by 1,2;
EOF
sqlite3 -header current.db < /work/ls.sql
sqlite3 -header current.db "select pool_code, route_key, profile_id, release_id, count(*) from logical_operations o join service_routes r using(route_id) join route_assignments ra on ra.route_id=o.route_id and o.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms and o.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms join worker_pools p on p.pool_id=ra.pool_id where r.service_id=2 and o.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 and o.opened_at_ms<1778155200000 group by 1,2,3,4;"
